clue.text: He throws women out of power, retaining Times

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other
out of here means the women are taken away from the word for power

parts.note: taken as the word itself
T is the abbreviation for time, doubled here for the plural

explanation.surface: A man ousts women from power while keeping hold of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He throws' is a person who shapes pots on a wheel. Times as TT is the abbreviation for time, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramicist shapes clay on a wheel, which is called throwing.

clue.text: Launch site for arrows — some ricochet

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used, its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A bit of ricochet happens at the place darts are thrown from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run of letters inside 'ricochet'. Arrows is slang for darts.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the line a player stands behind to throw is named with this word, and darts are called arrows.

clue.text: It has small hairy legs thanks to natural evolution

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: evolution suggests gradual change, so the letters of natural are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature owes its little hairy legs to nature's development.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: this spider's legs are hairy, if hardly small. TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: This large spider is known for its hairy legs.

clue.text: 8 revolutionary confectioners

definitions.note: 8 refers to the answer to 8 down, a reference book of words

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the sweet maker's name is read backwards

parts.note: Trebor is a British confectionery company, makers of mints

explanation.surface: A rebellious group of sweet makers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns TREBOR backwards. Le Robert is the leading French dictionary, which is what 8 means here.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Robert is the standard French lexicon, so it is an example of a wordbook.

clue.text: Industrial area sees reforms during changeover

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other

parts.note: the turn of the tide is a change of direction, so tide stands for the changeover

indicators.note: reforms means remakes, so the letters of sees are rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory region witnesses reorganisation at a time of transition.
explanation.walkthrough: Teesside is an industrial area in north-east England around the River Tees. A changeover as TIDE is loose: the tide's turn is a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around Middlesbrough is known for steel and chemical works.

clue.text: Anybody's 23, 8 and 1

definitions.note: the phrase is usually preceded by every, meaning anyone at all, so it fills in for anybody

parts.note: 23 across is Cruise, as in the actor Tom Cruise
8 down is a dictionary, and dick is old slang for a dictionary
taken as written
1 across is Potter, as in the boy wizard Harry Potter

explanation.surface: A themed roll call of first names, said to belong to anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: Each cross-reference gives the first name that goes with that answer. 'Dick' as slang for a dictionary is old (to swallow the dick is to use long words).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for ordinary people in general, anyone at all.

clue.text: Result of cold snap

definitions.meaning: being left out in freezing weather leads to this condition, as with hypothermia
a snap is a photograph, each frame of film being one of these

explanation.definitionFit: Being left out unprotected in the cold harms the body, and a single photographic frame is also called this.

clue.text: Small flies without number for swallows

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the theatre's flies and wings are both offstage areas, so flies stands for wings

explanation.surface: Tiny insects lacking a figure are mistaken for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallows is a verb here, gulps of drink, not the birds. In a theatre the flies and the wings are both offstage spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of drink, so it is a mouthful taken down.

clue.text: Short notice scrawled in journal, Johnson's work

indicators.note: in places the scrawled letters inside the journal

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: scrawled suggests messy writing, so the letters are jumbled
short means the word is cut off before its last letter

explanation.surface: A brief note is scribbled in a diary; it's the famous lexicographer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 dictionary of English, so 'Johnson's work' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's best-known achievement was his 1755 wordbook of English.

clue.text: Brucie danced with Henry and Mike, the little angels

indicators.note: danced suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Bruce Forsyth took to the dance floor with two partners, like little angels.
explanation.walkthrough: Brucie is the late British TV host Bruce Forsyth, who presented Strictly Come Dancing, hence the dancing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are child-like winged figures in art, and this is the Hebrew plural.

clue.text: Singer makes an impression on radio

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: prints are impressions made by pressing

explanation.surface: A vocalist leaves a mark when broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' says the answer sounds like PRINTS. Prince was the American singer of Purple Rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince was a famous American pop musician.

clue.text: Engineer insists Mick strips damaged car parts in vain

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so one group of letters is pushed into the other
engineer as a verb means contrive or rework, so the letters are rearranged
strips means the outer letters are peeled away, leaving the middle
damaged signals the letters of car are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mechanic is stripping a wrecked car for parts, and Mick is vain about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strips' leaves Mick's middle letters, which join the anagram of 'insists'; 'parts' then puts the jumbled 'car' inside that, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excessively in love with their own image is conceited.

clue.text: Astutely arranged nuts around new artist's work

indicators.note: around means the word for nuts goes round the other pieces

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
an oeuvre is the whole body of an artist's work

explanation.surface: Crazy people cleverly arranged a new body of art.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts is the adjective crazy, not the hardware or the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre is to steer things cleverly into position, a skilful arranging.

clue.text: Airline British switched to Asian capital …

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: switched means the two letters swap places

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British

explanation.surface: A British carrier changed its route to an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan. 'switched' just swaps the two letters, which for a pair is the same as reading them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku is the seat of government of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: … mad keen to fill up with increased fuel

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are filled with the other word, which sits inside them
mad suggests things in disorder, so the letters of keen are rearranged

parts.note: rose means went up, increased

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to fill up with more fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 13 across, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil burnt in lamps and jet engines is a fuel.

clue.text: Belief inspiring Catholic perceived banks to be beyond reproach

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a thing held beyond reproach

indicators.note: banks means borders on both sides, so the word for perceived goes round

parts.note: saw means perceived

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word for belief takes in a letter

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief

explanation.surface: A Catholic's faith borders on being untouchable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link. The setter said an edit adding 'an institution' before 'beyond reproach' was lost, which is why the definition reads as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution exempt from criticism.

clue.text: 8 rooms in the inn?

definitions.meaning: 8 refers to 8 down, a reference book of words
barristers work in rooms called this in the Inns of Court in London

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is a major British publisher of a wordbook, and barristers' offices at the Inns of Court bear the same name.

clue.text: David's friend put different hat on in winter

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the winter month

parts.note: January, abbreviated JAN, is a winter month

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts on another hat when it's cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Jonathan, son of King Saul, was David's close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, Saul's son was the devoted companion of David.

clue.text: Church recruits primitive cleric

indicators.note: recruits means takes in, so the church letters hold the other piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original

explanation.surface: A church takes on an old-fashioned clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: A curé is a French parish priest; ur- as primitive is the prefix seen in words like urtext.
explanation.definitionFit: A curé is a parish priest in France, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Shrinks back game

definitions.meaning: small birds that are shot or hunted, game birds

explanation.definitionFit: To flinch in fear is to cower, and the small bird is hunted as game.

clue.text: Tax office caught American where 23 lives

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
23 is Cruise, as in Tom Cruise, so his home is Tom's house

explanation.surface: An American is caught at the tax office where a film star lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across, CRUISE, points to the actor Tom Cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A customs house is the port building where duties on imports are collected.

clue.text: Row across river to German city

indicators.note: across means the word for row stretches over the river letter, holding it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone rows across a river to a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside TIER. Row is a line of seats, not rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany.

clue.text: Harry's not even frazzled

definitions.note: read as harry is, harry being a verb meaning to harass

indicators.note: not even means only the odd-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: Harry is not the slightest bit worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not even' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'frazzled'. Harry looks like a name but is the verb to harry.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them, and to disconcert someone is much the same.

clue.text: Clinton's first trick: send in one missile

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Clinton is used
send in means put the letter for one inside the trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's first move is a ploy: launch a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes C, and 'send in' puts I inside RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise missile is a guided weapon flying low over long distances.

clue.text: Croatian's out of place in Ulster

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are moved from their order

parts.note: the possessive is not a letter; the word is croatian

explanation.surface: A Croatian person feels like a stranger in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges CROATIAN. An ulster is a long, heavy overcoat, not the province.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, a garment for keeping off wet weather.

clue.text: I'd a year off about start of 70s? Could be

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
off means wrong, so the letters of a year are rearranged
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the 70s are the seventies, whose first letter is S

explanation.surface: Someone takes a year out around the beginning of the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns A YEAR into AREAY, split around S by 'about'. The 70s must be read as the word seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase grants that something may well be so, a hedged agreement.

clue.text: Jeffrey wasn't about to enrol guy with sharp teeth

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the enrolled letters are read from right to left
to enrol means to take in as a member, so the two names hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Jeffrey refuses to sign up a man with fangs.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Jeffrey' and 'wasn't' backwards; the apostrophe is ignored. The definition is playful: the man's sharp teeth belong to his saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber cutter works with a saw, whose blade bristles with sharp teeth.
